turns.input: $crumb I supervise a small commercial window-cleaning crew. At the end of a job, we often forget one of the photos the property manager expects and have to return. I want to see whether a tiny local tool could catch missing completion photos before we leave. I can introduce you to two other crew supervisors, but neither has agreed to a test. I have no app. Help me find the strongest first use and prepare the useful next step. Do not build or contact anyone yet.
turns.output:
The return trip is the useful clue: a missing photo only becomes expensive once the crew has left. I’ll pressure-test a departure check and prepare a small learning step around your own crew. The two introductions are possible routes, not agreed tests.


There’s a useful wrinkle: existing photo software already supports required-photo checklists. The strongest reason for your own tool would be a faster check at departure, with less setup. We still need to learn whether photos are forgotten, the manager’s requirements are unclear, or the photos are taken but hard to find.


I’ve prepared a departure card and a five-job learning plan. The key distinction is now explicit: “there’s a photo” doesn’t mean “it shows the view this manager required.” Your supervisor judgment stays in the check. I’ve also drafted a neutral interview invitation for the two introductions, without asking them to test an app.


I’d start with **your own crew, one recurring property, and a check immediately before departure**. The return trip gives this a concrete consequence.

CompanyCam already supports [required-photo checklists](https://help.companycam.com/en/articles/6828391-creating-a-checklist); its [Crew plan](https://help.companycam.com/en/articles/14477655-companycam-plans-explained) publicly lists USD 149/month for three users. A tiny local tool would need to earn its place through speed, simplicity and reliable offline use.

I prepared the [departure card and next-step pack](/<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-g1DiZ5/independent-retest/crumb-contexts/window-photo-20261006-a91f/next-step.md): a proposed five-job manual check, measures, a provisional tool brief, and an unsent invitation with five interview questions. Nothing was built or sent.

**My take:** ONE GAP before tool decision: can required shots be explicit and was the last failure omission rather than unclear requirements or delivery? Prepare a manual departure check; demand remains unproven. (Inference; source: Founder report; required-photo alternatives; next-step.md.)

**What we are building toward:** Find the strongest first use and prepare the next step for a tiny local completion-photo check; do not build or contact anyone.

**The first user:** Provisional first user: founder as supervisor at departure from one recurring commercial property with explicit manager photo requirements; recurrence/requirements need verification.

**Their pain:** Crews leave a commercial property without a completion photo its manager expects and must return to capture it.

**Evidence so far:** CompanyCam has required-photo fields; Crew publicly lists USD149/month for 3 users. Docs say checklist photos cannot be added offline until reconnection. No commercial omission-rate evidence found. (Reported; source: Opened 2026-10-06: help.companycam.com checklist/plans articles; URLs in next-step.md.) This does not establish demand.

**What could undo it:**

Presence cannot certify correct view or cleaning quality. Unknown requirements, unsafe recapture and lost local data undermine the promise; human review required. No outside demand or test consent. (Inference; source: Analysis of stated workflow; next-step.md.)

**Still unknown:**

A stable property shot list and a departure check under 60 seconds could help. These are hypotheses. Frequency, avoidable return-trip cost, phone/storage constraints and willingness to pay unknown. (Inference; source: Prepared bounded learning proposal, next-step.md.)

Does this capture the direction you agree with, including the doubts? Agreeing lets us keep investigating; it does not approve building.
